source_evidence.observation: The source defines the sub-gaussian norm by ∥X∥ψ₂ = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
The source states that any bounded random variable X is sub-gaussian and satisfies ∥X∥ψ₂ ≤ C∥X∥∞.
The constant in the displayed bound is specified as C = 1/√(ln 2).
The bounded-variable example imposes no mean-zero, symmetry, independence, or particular-distribution assumption.

hypotheses: X is bounded, so the source's infinity norm ∥X∥∞ is finite.
conclusions: X is a sub-gaussian random variable.
Its sub-gaussian norm satisfies ∥X∥ψ₂ ≤ C∥X∥∞, equivalently ∥X∥ψ₂ ≤ ∥X∥∞/√(ln 2).
definitions_and_conventions: The sub-gaussian norm is ∥X∥ψ₂ = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
The constant C in Equation (2.17) is exactly 1/√(ln 2).
The notation ∥X∥∞ is the infinity norm used to express boundedness of X.
implicit_context: X is considered in the chapter's probability-space setting, and E denotes expectation.
The logarithm in the constant is the natural logarithm.

details: The claim applies to every bounded random variable.
No centering, symmetry, independence, or distributional-form condition is required.
The conclusion is an upper bound for the ψ₂ norm in terms of the infinity norm.
The comparison is one-sided; equality is not asserted.
The bound uses C = 1/√(ln 2), not merely an unspecified absolute constant.
Sub-gaussianity is understood through Definition 2.5.6 and the exponential-square threshold 2 in Equation (2.13).

undebatable_constraints: The quantified object must be an arbitrary bounded random variable X.
The conclusion must include that X is sub-gaussian.
The inequality must have direction ∥X∥ψ₂ ≤ C∥X∥∞.
The ψ₂ norm must retain the source definition inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
No mean-zero, symmetry, independence, or special-distribution hypothesis may be added.
contracts.contract_plain_english: Every bounded random variable is sub-gaussian, and its sub-gaussian norm is at most its infinity norm divided by √(ln 2). No centering, symmetry, independence, or special distributional assumption is required.
